title: How Plot Works
use_cases: Use when outlining a story to ensure each plot point ties to character choice.
Use when designing character arcs that drive narrative tension.
Implement when creating conflict that propels the plot toward its conclusion.
Configure when balancing cause and effect to maintain reader engagement.
Use when distinguishing plot from simple fact recitation in a narrative.
Use when crafting decision moments that shape the storyline.
Use when planning world building elements that support plot decisions.
content:
Plot has a specific structure. It follows a format that sucks readers in; introduces characters, character arcs and development, and world building; and compels readers to keep reading in order to satisfy conflict and answer questions.

Plot is about cause and effect, but, most importantly, plot is about choice: a character’s choice.

In other words, the difference between plot and story is that a plot is not just the recitation of facts; the facts you include in your plot each have a purpose, putting a character into a situation where they must make a decision and pulling the story toward its conclusion.
